en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-jñānaprabhā-sarvakarmāvaraṇa-viśodhana-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Dharma Master, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was in the palace of the Sun and Moon Deva Kings.
Also present were Tathāgata Jñānaprabha, Tathāgata Bhūtārtha, and Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa-rāśi.
The Tathāgata Ghoṣeśvara, the Tathāgata Krodha, the Tathāgata Ratnacandra,
as well as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharaṇīdhara-rāja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
and others such as these, together with all those Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
together with all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
was within that palace, in the Pavilion of the Victorious Banner.
Each sat upon a lion throne adorned with Jambūnada gold;
they were majestic and magnificent, like mountains of gold, their radiant splendor shining brilliantly as they illuminated one another.
At that time, the Lord of the Palace, the Sun and Moon Devas,
beheld these Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas,
whose majestic power and brilliance surpassed all the gods.
Giving rise to a sense of rare wonder, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
standing before the Buddha, he reflected within himself:
"Now these Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas..."
This is indeed a lamp for the realm of all sentient beings;
it will surely be able to illuminate and shatter all evil darkness.
How may I further attain the transformative wisdom of dhāraṇī?
Born in the ten directions with such majesty and virtue,
you shall act as a light for all sentient beings.
At that time, the Tathāgata, along with all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, and others—
They all knew the thoughts in the mind of the Lord of the Palace, the Sun and Moon Deva King.

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Lord of the Palace, the Sun and Moon Deva King, saying: "Deva King, you should listen attentively; I shall now for your sake proclaim the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the dhāraṇīs."
At that time, the Lord of the Palace, the Sun and Moon Devas, received the instruction and listened.
He then spoke the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas: "Namo Jñānaprabhā Tathāgata; Namo Satyatathāgata."
Namo to the Tathāgata Golden Light Mass; namo to the Tathāgata King of Profound Sound;
namo to our Tathāgata Śākyamuni; namo to the Tathāgata Wrathful One; namo to the Tathāgata Jewel Moon.
Namo Samantabhadra Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. Namo Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. Namo Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
Furthermore, he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
*tadyathā | trya-dvi-na-ca-ru-na-na-ca-ru-pra-bha-du-ra-mi-cca-kā-ra-i-i-ti-taṃ-sa-su-ra-na-sa*.

the Blessed One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
That Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the Sun and Moon Devas, the Lords of the Palace, saying:
"Devas, this dhāraṇī was proclaimed together by eighty-eight koṭis of Buddhas of the past."
Out of great kindness and great compassion,
the Tathāgata now further proclaims this dhāraṇī, O Son of Heaven, for the purpose of protecting and benefiting all sentient beings.
It is subtle, wondrous, rare, difficult to encounter, and difficult to hear.
It is like the udumbara flower, which is rare and difficult to see;
it is also like the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world, which is rare and difficult to encounter.
This dhāraṇī is likewise so. O Son of Heaven,
if after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, at the time when the True Dharma is extinguished,
there should be sentient beings who commit the five heinous crimes;
They will certainly fall into the Avīci Hell.
However, if such a person encounters this dhāraṇī,
they will be able to purify their body and mind with courageous and firm resolve.
For twenty-one days and nights,
during three periods of the day and three periods of the night,
one should maintain the continuity of mind and mind-moments without allowing any interruption.
For those who recite these dharani phrases with a sincere mind and repent,
their karma of the immediate retribution will be extinguished without remainder.
Furthermore, O Son of Heaven, by the power of the majesty of these dharani phrases, such a person—
One could cause the Avīci Hell to shatter into a hundred pieces until not even a remnant remains,
and furthermore, enable the sentient beings within it who possess karmic offenses to also attain liberation.
Each and every one was reborn in Jambudvīpa in the south, obtaining human form and further gaining the knowledge that these were all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who,
by the power of the merit of the dhāraṇī, had rescued and delivered me.
How much more so for the karmic actions of the person who maintains and recites [this mantra].
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the Lord of the Palace, the Sun and Moon Deva Kings, saying:
"Son of Heaven, I too, desiring to bring benefit and peace to all sentient beings,
shall likewise recite this dhāraṇī during the final age and provide protection by proclaiming it."
In order that no humans or non-humans may be able to cause them affliction or disturbance,
he then spoke this dhāraṇī: Tadyathā | dunaḍi mahādunaḍi sūru ||

Having heard the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra speak these names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as well as the dhāraṇīs,
all the doubts within their hearts were completely severed.
Having resolved to attain bodhicitta and vowed never to regress, they rejoiced with leaping joy, prostrated, and withdrew.
*The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Light of Wisdom that Extinguishes All Karmic Obstructions*, spoken by the Buddha.
